transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-03-26
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Tomás (Redwood SE), Aisha (Cythera VP Platform), Ravi (SRE), Lena (Security), Oliver (Dev)

Auto Summary: Quick demo of org/project key approaches, discussion of quota models for multi-tenant traffic, RBAC and billing segmentation options, and an initial POC plan for Dedicated capacity. Security questions around KMS / audit trails, and a tentative next step to run a POC next week.

Topics covered: tenant access models, rate limiting patterns (burst vs sustained), fairshare vs capacity lanes, project key vs org key tradeoffs, billing segmentation, KV/prefix cache impacts on cost, SSO/KMS and audit requirements, POC scope and metrics.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro, I'm Maya, AE on the account, and Tomás is our SE who will walk through the console and the quota model.
[00:12] Aisha (Cythera): Hi, thanks. We have a short-ish agenda: we want to understand how Redwood would let us map our internal tenants (teams + external customers) to keys and quotas, and how billing and access controls work.
[00:22] Tomás (Redwood): Great, we'll do a short demo of the Console and then talk through patterns. One note — terminology can be a bit fuzzy, so when we say "org key" we mean a top-level key that can issue project keys and act as a billing anchor; "project key" is scoped narrower and useful for customers or services.
[00:38] Ravi (Cythera): Quick Q — we currently have a hybrid model: most traffic goes through our internal gateway to a k8s-hosted model, but we're evaluating dedicated capacity for steady inference (and hosted API for dev). Our main constraints are burst protection, cost predictability, and separation of logs for compliance.
[00:55] Maya (Redwood): Totally. We'll show both routing and quota controls so you can keep dev traffic on hosted and route production to Dedicated.
[01:05] Tomás (Redwood): Jumping into the Console — you can set rate limits at the org level, or create project-level quotas. People often combine: org-level soft quotas for overall spend, and project keys for per-tenant concurrency and burst windows.
[01:24] Oliver (Cythera): If we create a project key per customer, how do we handle per-customer billing? We need clear invoice lines.
[01:33] Tomás (Redwood): Two patterns: one is to have the org key be the billing entity and use project keys tagged with metadata for invoice grouping. The Console exposes cost breakdowns by key tag, so you can export csv for billing. The other is multi-org setup if customers must be totally siloed (different contracts).
[01:50] Lena (Cythera): About audit logs — we need immutable logs with user identity for every request. Does Redwood surface request-level logs in the private deployment? And is that compatible with our KMS/HSM for key wrapping?
[02:05] Tomás (Redwood): In Private and Dedicated, you get request traces and can ship logs to your SIEM. For KMS, we support customer-managed keys for secrets — wrapping provider depends on the deployment (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, or HSM integrations). Audit trail tie-in is supported; we'll share the SOC2 artifacts.
[02:22] Aisha (Cythera): Good. On quota behaviour — we have big spikes from some partners that, if not limited, blow out our bill. What's Redwood's approach to backpressure?
[02:33] Tomás (Redwood): We use token/leaky-bucket style counters per key with configurable burst window and sustained rate. There are also capacity lanes — you can reserve Dedicated capacity for VIP tenants so they get guaranteed throughput, and everything else is behind fairshare. Fallback policies let you route to lower-cost quantized variants if Dedicated is saturated.
[02:52] Ravi (Cythera): How deterministic is quota enforcement under high concurrency? We can't have soft enforcement that lets 10x bursts through for a minute.
[03:00] Tomás (Redwood): Enforcement is at the routing layer next to the runtime, so it's low-latency and deterministic — we try to avoid leaky implementations where bursts slip by. You can set hard concurrency caps and burst capacity separately.
[03:14] Maya (Redwood): I'll add that the Console shows a simulated policy impact — you can run a "what-if" on a traffic trace and see dropped tokens, estimated cost, and latency tail changes. That tool helped a customer rework their burst windows.
[03:27] Aisha (Cythera): Nice. Can we see an example policy?
[03:31] Tomás (Redwood): Sure — demo time. (screen-share noises) Here is an org policy: default 'sustained' 10 rps per project, burst 100 tokens with a 30s decay. For a VIP tag we pin a Dedicated lane with reserved 200 rps. You can also create sticky routing rules so requests from certain IP ranges or header tokens always hit the VIP lane.
[03:58] Oliver (Cythera): That sticky routing — does it depend on a cookie or header? We have mobile clients that can't hold long-lived cookies.
[04:06] Tomás (Redwood): We use header-based project keys or hashed device ids as sticky keys. For mobile, we recommend short-lived project keys minted by your auth service.
[04:16] Ravi (Cythera): What's the cost delta if we pin 2 GPUs for VIP lane vs letting requests be elastic?
[04:24] Maya (Redwood): Depends on utilization pattern. If VIPs are heavy and steady, reserved Dedicated is often cheaper per token because batching and KV cache improve throughput. If it's spiky and low utilization, hosted with throttles may be better. We'll include a modeled cost calc with your traffic profile.
[04:40] Lena (Cythera): On encryption, we need per-tenant data separation and encryption-in-transit+at-rest. Also an option to disable telemetry export to 3rd party logs.
[04:52] Tomás (Redwood): Private deployment supports customer-controlled network boundaries and controls for log egress. You can restrict what telemetry leaves and we can push only aggregated metrics if required.
[05:03] Aisha (Cythera): Ok, quick clarifying question — for internal teams we want lax quotas; for external partners we want hard caps and billing per-request. How to make the policy model flexible?
[05:14] Tomás (Redwood): You can build hierarchical policies: org defaults, project overrides, and route-level rules. Also, tags allow cost centers to be attached so billing is automatic. We also support quotas tied to usage windows (daily/monthly) if you need invoiceable caps.
[05:29] Ravi (Cythera): What about key sprawl — we fear many project keys floating around. Is there tooling to rotate, revoke, and auto-expire keys?
[05:36] Tomás (Redwood): Yes, the Console has a key lifecycle UI: rotate, revoke, set TTLs, and audit key usage. You can also mint ephemeral keys via API if you prefer ephemeral auth.
[05:47] Oliver (Cythera): How does the KV/prefix cache interact with multi-tenant fairness? If a tenant hits cache warm for long sessions, do they hog GPU memory?
[05:58] Tomás (Redwood): Good point. Our runtime isolates KV cache per model instance and can set per-tenant cache quotas. We also have eviction strategies that free low-recently-used keys. In Dedicated pools you can pin cache sizes per lane.
[06:14] Aisha (Cythera): Can you walk through a simple POC plan where we push our typical 5-min burst patterns?
[06:20] Maya (Redwood): Sure. Proposed POC: 7 days, dedicated staging pool mirrored to your region, ingest your traffic trace, run with two policy sets (org-pinned VIPs vs project-key-per-customer), measure tail latency (95/99), cost per token, and cache hit rate. We then iterate.
[06:38] Ravi (Cythera): For the traffic trace ingestion, does Redwood need raw requests or synthetic replay?
[06:44] Tomás (Redwood): We can replay synthetic traces derived from your telemetry. If you can provide anonymized logs with headers + token counts and timestamps, that's enough. We also offer a small client for live traffic shadowing.
[06:55] Lena (Cythera): On the security questionnaire — does Redwood support SAML/SSO for the Console? And can we enforce RBAC so only allowed users can create org keys?
[07:07] Tomás (Redwood): Yes SAML/SSO + SCIM provisioning are available. RBAC is granular: you can limit key creation, quota editing, and visibility. We'll send the entitlement matrix.
[07:18] Aisha (Cythera): Can we do per-tenant data retention controls? For example some customers require shorter retention of prompts/logs.
[07:25] Tomás (Redwood): You can set retention policies by tag or project, or opt out of storing prompts entirely for certain keys. In Private, that's enforced on your side too.
[07:34] Maya (Redwood): Quick aside — one pattern we recommend: use org key to manage billing and master config, issue project keys per external customer with TTL and a tag for billing. Internal services can be under a separate project namespace with higher burst windows.
[07:50] Ravi (Cythera): If we do that, is there a chance project keys get used in ways to bypass org-level throttles?
[07:57] Tomás (Redwood): Policies are evaluated in order: org hard caps apply first, then project overrides can relax but not exceed hard org limits unless you explicitly allow it. We can also set a guardrail that enforces cost thresholds.
[08:12] Oliver (Cythera): Any gotchas with SDKs and token handling for mobile apps?
[08:17] Tomás (Redwood): Keep tokens short-lived, use your auth service to mint ephemeral tokens, and use header-based identification rather than embedding keys in app bundles.
[08:26] Aisha (Cythera): Let's talk about billing visibility — can we get per-route and per-model cost dashboards to attribute costs to product teams?
[08:34] Tomás (Redwood): Yes, Console has cost dashboards broken down by key, route, model, and time window. You can export csv and hook to your billing pipeline.
[08:43] Maya (Redwood): We're about to show a short simulation — what-if you set per-project daily caps and a VIP lane; watch how the simulated request queue fills and which requests get routed to fallback models.
[08:55] (screen share; simulated heatmap noises)
[09:03] Tomás (Redwood): See here — the simulation highlights red when queue delay exceeds threshold; you can tune burst window or enable fallback to a quantized variant that uses less memory and costs less per token.
[09:16] Ravi (Cythera): For fallback model quality differences, can we set automatic evals to monitor regressions if fallback is used more than X%?
[09:25] Tomás (Redwood): Yes — Redwood Optimize can run evals on a prompt set and alert if quality drops past a threshold tied to a rollout or fallback usage. Another option is canary routing where a small percentage uses the quantized model first.
[09:39] Lena (Cythera): We may require additional logging of user identities in audit records. Is that supported without leaking PII?
[09:46] Tomás (Redwood): We can log identity tokens or hashed IDs, and you control retention and redaction rules. We'll align on a hashed-ID scheme so PII isn't stored.
[09:57] Aisha (Cythera): Ok this has been super helpful. Couple of follow-ups: 1) cost modeling with our trace; 2) the POC scope; 3) security artifact handoff.
[10:07] Maya (Redwood): Yep — we'll send an email summarizing those items.
[10:11] Oliver (Cythera): One last question — if a tenant starts DOSing the API, are there automated mitigations beyond rate limiting? e.g., IP blacklists or token revocation?
[10:20] Tomás (Redwood): You can revoke keys instantly and block IP ranges at the gateway; additionally, our autoscaler has rules to shed non-VIP traffic under overload. We also integrate with WAFs for known bad actors.
[10:33] Ravi (Cythera): Great. Can you also confirm latency SLOs if we run on Dedicated? We need 95th < 120ms for small prompts.
[10:41] Tomás (Redwood): For short prompts on our Dedicated pools we can hit 95th under 100-120ms depending on model and sequence length. We'll include measured samples from similar customers.
[10:51] Maya (Redwood): Quick recap and blockers: Cythera to share traffic trace + security constraints. Redwood to share pricing, KV-cache benchmarks, and SOC2 artifacts. Agree on 7-day POC start target next week if logs available.
[11:07] Aisha (Cythera): Sounds good. If you can include a short example config showing org policy + project override that'd help our infra team.
[11:14] Tomás (Redwood): Will do — I'll paste a sample YAML with policy precedence and an example of sticky routing rules.
[11:21] Maya (Redwood): Cool — thanks everyone. We'll follow up in email and set up the POC kickoff.
[11:26] (meeting ends)
